elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: "Sparkling may assign this Agreement ... without consent to an affiliate"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business"

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: "Neither party may assign this Agreement ... without the written consent of the other party" (Garman's carve-out is not granted)

elements.element: Consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed"

elements.element: Vendor never to assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "Garman shall not assign this Agreement to any competitor of Sparkling"

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "No change of control of Sparkling shall constitute an assignment or give Garman any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors (i.e., Vendor also may assign to a successor without consent) with written notice
elements.evidence: only "Sparkling may assign ... without consent to an affiliate or to a successor"; Garman remains consent-bound

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed"

offending_extra_words: No change of control of Sparkling shall constitute an assignment
reasons: All atomic elements of the locked preferred level are satisfied: affiliate and successor carve-out for Sparkling (Customer), Vendor consent requirement retained, reasonableness standard, competitor bar for Garman, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.
Fallback is not independently satisfied (Garman is given no reciprocal notice-only successor assignment right), but that is irrelevant since preferred is met and the levels are separate bargains.

Minimality fails: the edit rewrites the whole of (d) (27 words to 115 words; official gates on length ratio and changed-character ratio both failed) and adds terms beyond what the preferred level needs — "in whole or in part", "reorganization", "or business", "or delayed", the deemed-assignment sentence, and remedies "suspend or re-price" that go past the required 'no termination right'.

Tighten to a short proviso, e.g. add after "other party": ", which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld; provided that Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, and Garman may not assign to a competitor of Sparkling; a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and gives Garman no termination right."

Intent is preserved: unrelated restrictions in (c) remain effective and are only opened by a cross-reference; verify that paragraph (d) actually sits in Section 20 so the new "as permitted by Section 20(d)" reference does not dangle.
